agents.name: Automation
agents.summary: Turns the captured Tagging log + your plain-English policy into an autonomous workflow — tags, ACR changes, wait periods, and a scheduled loop that runs every few hours. Plans first, then executes when armed.

agents.name: Ensemble Report
agents.summary: Sphinx — the estate brain, built from Release the Hounds. Summarises every hound's released result (page cache + the Nemesis / Atlas / Sköll snapshots) into one story: how exposed the estate is and what the risk is made of, where it concentrates (by hound, on assets, in time), the cross-hound overlaps no single hound sees, blind spots, ranked next moves and which hounds the picture was built from. Every number links to the hound that owns it. Needs a release; reads caches only, never navi.db.

agents.name: Certificates
agents.summary: Certania — finds expired certificates month by month over the last 12 months (plus everything older) and those failing in the next 12 months, and tags their assets Cert failure : <Mon>-<DD>-<YYYY>. Expiry timeline, crown jewels, weak crypto and self-signed metrics, Cert Issue tagging by plugin, and an IoT/app cache fingerprinted from certs. Deterministic — no free-form LLM reasoning.

agents.name: Dashboard Builder
agents.summary: Describe any view in plain English and the model writes a read-only navi.db query, then renders it in the project style as KPI tiles, a bar chart, or a table. Visualize something we didn't build a page for — without leaving the app.

agents.name: Device Discovery
agents.summary: Four cooperating agents: discover IoT devices, harvest carrier plugins, cross-term hunt the population, and learn new detections (HITL).

agents.name: Criticality Calibration
agents.summary: Adjust Asset Criticality Rating per tag (set / +N / −N) with a business justification; bulk via natural language.

agents.name: Classification
agents.summary: Classifies every asset by WHAT IT IS — Windows / Linux / macOS / IoT (by device type) / OT / Network / Virtual / Cloud / Unclassified — to close the asset-detection loop that stalls ownership. Uses the 'no software enum = not IoT' rule, overlays ownership + risk per class, turns the Unclassified bucket into a reason-tagged worklist, and writes gated Class:<type> tags.

agents.name: Custom App Discovery
agents.summary: Finds software missing from inventory via routes/paths; tag custom apps in plain English ('Tag my custom app navi').

agents.name: ATT&CK Mapping
agents.summary: Tags assets by the ATT&CK impact of their vulnerabilities: fetches the live ATT&CK→CVE mapping and tags every asset whose findings cite a mapped CVE with its Primary/Secondary Impact + Exploit Technique, via navi's tag-by-CVE selector.

agents.name: AI Inventory
agents.summary: Content-first AI/ML discovery — the Tenable AI plugin family plus the software & cpes inventories, plugin output, and network endpoints. Classifies each asset by role; metrics for footprint (share of estate, found beyond the AI plugins), exposure (exposed / unauth endpoints, shadow egress), risk (KEV, critical, EOL, MITRE ATLAS) and governance (ACR vs the role's suggested ACR, already tagged). Per-row 🔍 Why + false-positive suppression. Tags assets AI, AI Role, AI Software, AI Exposed, AI Priority, AI Egress, AI ATLAS (gated) and sets ACR by AI Role (gated).

agents.name: End of Life
agents.summary: Charon — finds the assets running Unsupported or End-of-Life software (lifecycle text in the plugin name, so it expands as new EOL plugins appear) and tags them: Lifecycle:<Unsupported|End of Life> (navi tag-by-name) and by end-of-life date Lifecycle EOL:<YYYY-MM-DD>. Product view: OS vs application, years past end of life, crown jewels, KEV and critical overlap.

agents.name: Identity Inventory
agents.summary: Janus — finds human, service/NHI and machine identities by content (local-user enumeration plugins + output), classified by external authority (Microsoft well-known SIDs/RIDs, AD $ accounts, Linux UID convention). Metrics for inventory, credential coverage, account hygiene (privileged, account reuse, never-expiring, SSH passwords) and priority (privileged on exploitable hosts, KEV, crown jewels). Tags the hosting assets: Identity, NHI, Machine ID, Owner, Identity Risk, Identity Coverage (gated), plus natural-language tagging.

agents.name: Scan Health
agents.summary: Chronos — what your scans can and can't see. Per asset: credential health from the Target Credential Status / Issues plugins (104410 failed, 110385/102094 insufficient privilege, 117885 intermittent, 110723 none provided, 141118/110095 OK) and plugin 19506, patch-assessment failures (21745), scan freshness, agent vs network, crown-jewel blind spots. Per scanner / policy / scan: time per asset, load share, credential success, Nessus version and plugin-feed currency, safe-checks off. Tags the exact assets under Scan Health (gated). Can run for the whole estate or for one tag's assets (switch between them; tag writes stay inside the tag).

agents.name: SLA Tracker
agents.summary: Sköll — remediation adherence + open-vuln aging vs the SLA clock, segmented by owner/tag. Emailable dashboard; records a daily snapshot for trending.

agents.name: Tag Removal
agents.summary: Garmr — lists every tag in the tenant and removes the ones you choose (queued to the Tagging log as -remove). Your choices can feed the AI Contract, which removes them first, forces a 30-min pause + navi update, then re-runs the tagging workflow.

agents.name: Agent Group Sync
agents.summary: Sirius — tags every asset in a Tenable agent group with Agent Group:<name>. Three ways: give a list of group names (NL), tick groups in a widget, or tag every group at once (navi enrich tag --group).

agents.name: CISA KEV
agents.summary: Laelaps — CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities on your assets, joined to CISA's catalog: remediation due dates (overdue / due soon), ransomware use, crown jewels and vendors. Tags assets CISA KEV:Vulnerable (xref), by catalog date added, by CISA due date (CISA KEV Due:<YYYY-MM-DD>) and CISA KEV:Ransomware. Plus an NL→SQL to hunt KEV in navi.db / tags.

agents.name: Software Inventory
agents.summary: Mines the software table for version sprawl (one product at many versions), the most-deployed software, standardized vs fragmented apps, and rare single-install software — and tags any product or version (gated).

agents.name: Post-Quantum
agents.summary: Heimdall — one ▶ Run reads certificate crypto (RSA / ECC / DSA are broken by Shor), TLS/SSH key exchange, OpenSSH/OpenSSL versions and Tenable's Post-Quantum plugins (277650 / 277652 / 277653). Metrics: share of the estate quantum-vulnerable, certificates still valid at the CNSA 2.0 deadlines (2030 / 2033), harvest-now exposure, legacy stacks, crown jewels and KEV overlap. Ranks a migration roadmap and tags the assets: Post-Quantum, PQC Priority, PQC Risk, PQC Harvest-Now, PQC Transport, PQC Agility.

agents.name: Attack Paths
agents.summary: Fenrir — chains the weaknesses Tenable already found into ranked paths to the crown jewels: remote exploits, local privilege escalation, credentials shared across hosts, NTLM relay, domain-controller flaws and failed compliance controls (LAPS, SMB signing, LLMNR, WDigest, sudo). Interactive attack map, diverse routes per crown jewel, choke points and a remediation bundle that cuts the most exposure. Reachability is inferred (no flow data). Gated tagging: Attack Path : Entry Point | Pivot | Target | Choke Point.

agents.name: Web App Scanning
agents.summary: Arachne — consolidated WAS overview + per-app scan reports: severity, OWASP Top-10, tech stack, scan coverage. Two dashboards over the apps/findings tables, with a jump nav; every metric, severity/OWASP bar, tech chip and tag cohort opens the matching apps in Web App Recon.

agents.name: Web App Dossier
agents.summary: Beagle — the WAS asset deep-dive. Point it at a web app and it maps the terrain from navi's info plugins: sitemap, scan telemetry, target facts, screenshot, external URLs, cookies, methods — every plugin clickable to its raw stored output. Argos for web apps; launched from the WAS dashboards — a widget link (?f=sev:critical, owasp:A3, tech:PHP, scan:stale…) narrows the app list to that group.

agents.name: Compliance Overview
agents.summary: Minos — judges the estate against its audit benchmarks. Consolidated compliance over the compliance table: pass/fail/warning, the controls failing the most assets, framework rollup (NIST/PCI/HIPAA/CIS/ISO), and per-asset scorecards. Assign an Audit Owner to a control's failing assets. Grouped metric cards and a jump nav; every card, status bar, failing control, framework and benchmark opens the matching assets in the Compliance Deep-Dive.

agents.name: Compliance Drill-down
agents.summary: Tiresias — the compliance detective, two lenses over the same data. By Asset: point it at one asset for every audit check it passed/failed/warned (actual vs expected, framework mappings) plus the inferred link between a failed control and the real vulns backing it, which you can tag. By Audit File: the same estate through the benchmark — an audit-file leaderboard, per-file adherence, the checks and assets each file covers, and the real vulns backing its failing controls, at aggregate and per file. Launched from Minos — a widget link (?f=st:failed, check:<id>, fw:<framework>, audit:<file>, pct:lt50) narrows the asset list to that group and opens its worst asset.

agents.name: Audit Authoring
agents.summary: Draco — the lawgiver. Author a custom Tenable .audit file two ways: describe the check in plain English and Claude drafts valid Nessus checks, or build one field-by-field from the platform catalog — Windows config (registry, password/lockout/audit policy, user rights, service, REG_CHECK, WMI, PowerShell), Windows file-content (FILE_CONTENT_CHECK), and Unix/Linux/macOS (file, content, command, RPM, process, service). Live .audit preview, syntax validation, and auto-mapped framework references (NIST/PCI/HIPAA/CIS/ISO). Download a scan-ready .audit or a single check. NEW: seed a whole CIS benchmark from the built-in library (CIS Docker, Ubuntu, RHEL) and adjust controls in one prompt (e.g. “create a CIS Docker benchmark and tighten 5.x”).

agents.name: Asset Dossier
agents.summary: Give it one asset UUID or IP and it returns the whole story: risk band, the pack's tags deciphered (what each one means + which Hound raised it), severity breakdown, top CVEs, software and certs — plus live navi explore uuid views.

agents.name: Notify & Reports
agents.summary: The loop-closer. Turns the pack's findings into owner-routed remediation, KEV fire-alarms, cert countdowns, and morning briefings — emailed to the right humans with deep-links back into the Tenable platform. Reads Atlas Owner: tags to send each owner only THEIR assets. Preview first; sending is double-gated (writes + email + confirm).

agents.name: Explorer › Assets
agents.summary: Search navi.db assets by hostname, IP, OS or network. Read-only navi.db search via the UI.

agents.name: Alerts
agents.summary: Alert Raven watches navi.db for conditions worth waking a human — credentialed-scan coverage drops, scans over 3 hours, new CISA KEV, expiring certs, new criticals and more. Like the raven that rides with the wolf pack and calls out where the danger is, it reports alert metrics, suggests patterns to alert on, lets you craft an alert in plain English and TEST it before saving, then emails a digest when something fires. Alerts fire on change (once, until they clear); evaluation runs in the AI Contract loop; email delivery is gated (NAVI_EMAIL).

agents.name: Explorer › Vulnerabilities
agents.summary: Search findings by plugin name, ID, CVE, or severity — grouped by plugin. Read-only navi.db search via the UI.

agents.name: Explorer › Plugins
agents.summary: Every distinct plugin in navi.db — search by ID, name, or family. Read-only navi.db search via the UI.

agents.name: Exposure Routes
agents.summary: Pulls users & groups (navi primary, Tenable MCP backup) split into paginated Users/Groups, tracks ownership COVERAGE (how much of the attack surface has an owner — an asset is 'closed' only when every route it sits on is owned), and maps exposure routes & paths to owners from plain English — tagging Owner:<group/user> on every asset on the matched route/path (gated).

agents.name: Ownership
agents.summary: Ownership from the ASSET's point of view (Terminus). Three layers — business leaders (Business Owner: groups of assets/apps), technology owners (Owner: routes & paths, from Atlas), and a single complete Asset Owner who owns an asset's every route & path (or 'the rest'). Shows per-asset ownership %, what's unclaimed / blind, crown jewels (ACR >= 9) and what the Hounds already know about them, mitigated/accepted/ignored share, and assigns owners from plain English that reads each asset's tags. All writes gated.

agents.name: Explorer › Routes
agents.summary: Application routes from navi.db (vuln_route) — search by app name or type. Read-only navi.db search via the UI.

agents.name: MCP Routing Reference
agents.summary: Tenable MCP vs navi MCP — a capability & routing matrix, the limits that force a handoff (rule-tag cap, OS/app/device detection, ACR/AES, dashboards), and a navi-side snapshot to sanity-check the connection.

agents.name: Explorer › Paths
agents.summary: Filesystem paths discovered on assets (vuln_paths) — search by path text. Read-only navi.db search via the UI.

agents.name: Exposure Score
agents.summary: The pack's convergence page (Nemesis). Fuses every Hound's signal into ONE exposure score per asset — KEV+EPSS+VPR+ACR+AES and open-finding SLA aging direct, plus attack path (Fenrir), identity (Janus: account reuse > other NHI / identity risk), AI (Pythia), EOL (Charon), weak/expiring crypto (Certania+Heimdall), ATT&CK (Orthrus) and ownership (Terminus) from tags. Grouped estate / convergence / confidence metrics, an at-a-glance strip and a jump nav; ranks the estate worst-first, surfaces the worst finding from each Hound and where they converge, and turns a remediation play into a projected reduction. Cached on disk per navi.db + weighting and built in the background — for the whole estate or for one tag's assets (a separate cache; switch between them). Priority tagging is gated and recomputed server-side.

agents.name: Explorer › Fixed
agents.summary: Search the fixed table — remediation history + Pass/Fail SLA verdicts. Filter by severity, state, and SLA outcome. Read-only navi.db search.

agents.name: Remote Remediation
agents.summary: Amarok — the pack's troubleshooting and remediation executor over navi action push (SSH to Linux hosts, navi.db assets or ANY IP / hostname / small CIDR). Built-in read-only diagnostics (Quick health incl. the host's public egress IP, network, security posture, Tenable agent, resources), credential tests that tell auth failures from unreachable / port closed / DNS / timeout / a CHANGED host key, 'does this path exist?' (stat + sha256), AI-assisted remediation (Tenable's Solution → strict JSON plan → deterministic validator → canary-first deploy with per-step verify and rollback), and free-form commands / file pushes / armed campaigns. Every remote action is TRIPLE-gated (writes + NAVI_REMOTE_CODE_EXECUTION + confirm); every command on every host lands in the hash-chained C2 log (never the reply). Other hounds hand paths and vulns over via sessionStorage — pre-filled, never auto-run.

agents.name: Explorer › Web Apps
agents.summary: Search the WAS apps table — filter by name/target/tech, severity presence, and scan recency. Parsed tech + top OWASP per app. Read-only navi.db search.

agents.name: Explorer › Compliance
agents.summary: Search every audit result in navi.db — by check, audit file, framework, status, or asset (host / IP). Failed first, with actual vs expected, the fix, and the framework references. Read-only navi.db search.

agents.name: Explorer › Software
agents.summary: Zero-day hunting over the software inventory — where a product is installed, at which versions, and which assets fall in an affected version range, each with its Nemesis exposure score (sort most-exposed first). ✨ Look up a new CVE (you approve every site it reads) to get the affected products and versions. Read-only navi.db search.

agents.name: Explorer › Tags
agents.summary: Search navi.db tags by category or value — asset counts per tag, plus a drill-down joined to the assets table showing exactly which assets carry each tag. Read-only navi.db search.
